purpose: Check Windows channel backpressure and recovery across a spawn/exit burst.
behavior: Prepares 1024 short hostname roots with merged stderr and a minimal environment, accumulating Spawn frames before reading any replies.
Writes on a separate thread and requires a one-second stalled write callback within sixty seconds, showing reply pressure propagated to host writes.
After reading resumes, requires every Spawned and Exited, joins the writer, and verifies subsequent Stop, Release and new Spawn work.
contracts: The burst represents roughly twice the 1024 reply budget because each root also yields Exited; host pipe buffers are deliberately 4 KiB.
dependencies: windows_host.rs Writer and Prepared requests; native hostname.exe; windows/queues.rs admission policy.
failures_or_limits: The full 4096-tree cap is tested separately with a lowered unit-test cap, not by this burst. Dropped output readers may make children fail writes; this case verifies channel delivery, not output success. It was not run.

purpose: Implement Windows test-child roles for argument recovery, stdio, Job containment and racing descendants.
behavior: Reruns an ignored exact test and emits raw command line, decoded argv, cwd/env, stdin handle type/byte count, output markers or chosen unsigned exit code.
Queries its innermost Job limits and attempts a CREATE_BREAKAWAY_FROM_JOB child to report whether escape was refused.
Builds optional resistant descendant chains, an early-exiting root, or a nested Job; a breeding role starts children only after CTRL_BREAK and logs each PID plus creation time at spawn.
contracts: Logged creation identity covers children created but not scheduled before forced termination; markers signal readiness to the parent oracle.
dependencies: windows_host.rs selects child test; windows_tree.rs consumes chain/breed/nest roles; Windows console and Job APIs.
failures_or_limits: Hanging Windows roles have no self-expiry watchdog in this file and rely on Job/process cleanup by tests. Reported historical runner counts in comments are not evidence from this analysis.

purpose: Provide a Windows named-pipe protocol host and disposable sub-host controls for supervisor integration tests.
behavior: Creates a first-instance local-only overlapped pipe, starts the supervisor on a windowless console, verifies connecting PID and exact Ready, and decodes into a bounded 64-frame receive channel.
Uses request IDs with unmatched-frame storage, ten-second frame/write bounds, DuplicateHandle close-source transfers, and Stop/List/Exit/handle-count helpers.
Sub-host modes expose a resistant tree for host death or channel flooding; a console mode checks graceful tree stop followed by a host-console event control.
contracts: A stalled host reader must backpressure the real supervisor; test Host Drop kills its supervisor so owned Jobs close.
dependencies: windows_os.rs supplies overlapped I/O and OS Proc oracles; windows_host/spawn.rs builds requests; windows_child.rs implements roles.
failures_or_limits: The early-message vector can grow and Drop only requests supervisor kill, without waiting here. Flood intentionally parks indefinitely after a stalled write until the parent kills the sub-host. These are test-specific lifetime choices.

purpose: Build Windows pipe Spawn requests with transferred handles and expose the resulting test tree.
behavior: Spec defaults to current environment/cwd, null stdin, separate stderr and 1000 ms grace; child mode prefixes the exact ignored test arguments.
prepare creates pipe ends, immediately transfers child-side handles into the supervisor and encodes OS strings into protocol bytes with no PTY.
spawn sends the prepared message, requires zero returned PTY handles, opens the root through the independent OS oracle and exposes stdout/stderr/stdin.
contracts: Prepared already owns remote handles before its message is sent; Host::give uses DUPLICATE_CLOSE_SOURCE.
dependencies: windows_host.rs communication and transfer; windows_os.rs Proc/Lines; omni_proto Spawn/Slot.
failures_or_limits: Dropping an unsent Prepared closes local ends but this type has no remote-handle rollback; those handles depend on later supervisor cleanup. This is fixture construction, not public host spawn behavior, and was not executed.

purpose: Provide Windows OS identity/liveness oracles, bounded observations and overlapped test transport primitives.
behavior: Checks logged PID plus creation time to distinguish a departed process from PID reuse; Proc holds a process handle for live/exit-code/termination and same-object handle checks.
Runs overlapped operations with a separate event, cancels on an optional timeout and waits for completion before releasing buffers.
A write-watching helper reports a stall then waits for eventual completion; line helpers preserve unmatched markers and bound requested observations by ten seconds.
contracts: Death assertions use native handles or creation identity rather than supervisor List alone.
failures_or_limits: The heading saying every wait is bounded is broader than implementation: limit None and post-stall GetOverlappedResult waits are indefinite, and the callback may never return. Lines is unbounded and stops silently on read error; Proc::alive treats wait statuses other than WAIT_TIMEOUT as nonalive.

purpose: Specify the ConPTY integration path, interrupt/resize behavior, stop timing and build-dependent handle retention.
behavior: Checks a prompt response, typed Ctrl-C exit, reported initial/resized dimensions, Closed resize after stop, and Invalid sizes zero or above 32767.
Uses a resistant writing descendant to require Stop and stream EOF within 1500 ms for a 1000 ms grace, both after root exit and while the root is live; the writer must be dead.
Repeats natural exit/EOF for 200 sessions, requiring all forty numbered markers plus END and measuring settled supervisor handles with a live-terminal control.
Checks no terminal event reaches the host console, then requires one direct console event control.
contracts: Reads PTY ends from Spawned, keeping output draining while terminal close may wait.
dependencies: windows_pty_term.rs role and Screen helpers; windows_host.rs; RtlGetVersion supplies build selection.
failures_or_limits: The handle assertion permits one extra handle per session below build 26100 plus ten slack, and ten slack on newer builds; it is not zero-leak evidence for older builds. Timing, build behavior and run outputs remain unexecuted.

purpose: Implement the Windows terminal test host, output-handle transfer and controlled console programs.
behavior: Sends terminal Spawn with zero stdio handles, pulls output first with DUPLICATE_CLOSE_SOURCE and starts Screen draining before obtaining the input end.
Runs prompt, burst, hang and size-polling roles, plus a stubborn writer whose armed marker precedes root exit or wait.
The writer ignores Ctrl-C/Break and blocks in close handling while producing ticks, enabling tests of independent force deadlines.
A separate console host clears its Ctrl-C ignore flag, counts events during two terminal sessions and raises a direct control event afterwards.
contracts: Term owns OS root identity, readable Screen and writable input; expected terminal control exit is 0xC000013A.
dependencies: windows_host.rs transport; screen.rs marker observation; Windows console APIs and child test entry.
failures_or_limits: Input write and internal armed-line/child waits are blocking fixture operations; resistant roles rely on parent Job termination. Source comments about OS close timing are contextual claims, not reproduced observations here.

purpose: Capture ConPTY output and find ordered visible-text markers for the integration oracle.
behavior: A reader thread appends raw bytes, records EOF/error time, and wakes condition-variable waiters.
Marker and value searches start after the previous match and wait up to the shared bound; end requires EOF and no read error.
The visible filter decodes lossily, strips CR and escapes, maps cursor-right to at most 512 spaces and cursor-position to a newline.
contracts: visible is a marker-oriented projection rather than a terminal screen emulator.
dependencies: windows_pty_term.rs owns Screen; windows_pty.rs uses markers, complete text and end timestamps.
failures_or_limits: Raw output grows without a cap and each search rebuilds visible text. The filter omits cursor overwrite/state semantics and loosely ends OSC on ESC plus any following character, so it cannot validate arbitrary terminal rendering or exact byte preservation.
